LHX.sentence: L3Harris is down slightly, but the real story is management's push to fix its skinny profit margins — they run leaner than the bigger defense contractors, and closing that gap is what everyone's watching.

ASML.sentence: ASML ticked up again, which is business as usual — they're the only company making a certain essential chipmaking machine, and the AI boom keeps demand strong.

LIN.sentence: Linde is quiet — industrial gas demand is steady and it's now priced about the same as its closest rival, which is a little unusual since it typically commands a premium.

MSFT.sentence: Microsoft has quietly pulled far ahead of its peers over the past month as investors piled in on the AI cloud story — the shares are running hot, but nothing dramatic changed in the business.

TMO.sentence: Thermo Fisher slipped a bit, but biotech funding is thawing again, and since more lab funding eventually means more orders for their equipment, better days may be a couple of quarters out.

ENB.sentence: Enbridge is barely moving — the pipeline toll-road business is steady, though the income it pays out is a bit skinny right now compared to safer alternatives.

NOW.sentence: ServiceNow bounced today but is still well below its high; big companies and government agencies keep signing on for its workflow-automation and AI tools, so the business is fine even as the stock cooled off.

GLNCY.sentence: Glencore dipped with commodity prices — this miner and trading house sits right in the middle of its cycle, neither cheap enough to be a screaming bargain nor expensive enough to worry about.

RDDT.sentence: Reddit jumped today and its advertising business is still growing fast, but the stock remains far below its high because of the lingering worry that Google could send it fewer visitors.

KOF.sentence: Coca-Cola FEMSA drifted down a little; it bottles Coke across Latin America, so its ups and downs mostly track the Mexican peso, which is sitting in a normal range.

PBR.A.sentence: Petrobras edged up with oil prices staying comfortably high, which keeps its very large dividend well-funded — the main risk is always Brazilian government meddling, not the oil itself.

AMKBY.sentence: Maersk, the container-shipping giant, had a big jump today and is now trading below the value of its own ships, though after such a sharp move it looks a touch stretched in the short term.

MA.sentence: Mastercard is up a little and actually trading cheaper than Visa right now, which is unusual given it's the faster-growing of the two — people keep tapping their cards more than ever.

ISRG.sentence: The da Vinci surgical robot maker was flat while similar medical-device stocks rallied, and that lag looks like nervous selling rather than any real sign hospitals are doing fewer procedures with their machines.
